fi-synchiropus-ocellatus.title: Scooter Dragonet (Scooter Blenny)
fi-synchiropus-ocellatus.summary: Despite the trade name it is a dragonet (family Callionymidae), not a blenny. It hops over sand and rock hunting tiny animals.
rows: About 5 in; wild record 8.9 cm (3.5 in) TL (FishBase)
More than one can be kept if added together, ideally 2–3 females per male
Carnivore. Sifts sand and rock for tiny animals; finely chopped meaty foods or enriched brine shrimp may be accepted
Pacific Ocean: from Indonesia to the Pitcairn Group; north to Japan; south to Australia
notes: Needs a mature reef with lots of live rock and a sand bed for natural food.

fi-synchiropus-stellatus.title: Red Scooter Dragonet (Starry Dragonet)
fi-synchiropus-stellatus.summary: A small, peaceful dragonet from the Indian Ocean that hops along the sand and rock picking off tiny crustaceans. It does best in a mature reef tank with lots of live pods.
rows: Tiny live foods: copepods and amphipods from the tank; some learn frozen foods. Adding live pods helps
Indian Ocean: East Africa to Indonesia, on reefs to about 40 m
notes: Best in a mature tank with plenty of live rock and sand, without fast, competing bottom feeders.

fi-trichonotus-setiger.title: Spotted Sand Diver
fi-trichonotus-setiger.summary: A slender, sand-dwelling fish that hovers in loose groups over sandy slopes picking plankton from the water, and dives headfirst into the sand when frightened.
rows: Lives in groups in the wild
Zooplankton picker: offer small meaty foods such as mysis and enriched brine shrimp
Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Queensland, Australia, over sand near reefs
notes: Needs an open, soft sand bed deep enough to dive into.
